import pandas as pd

# Read source tables with index_col=0 to ignore the numerical index column
source0 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length3_70/training_0.csv", index_col=0)
source1 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length3_70/training_1.csv", index_col=0)

# Perform the join on 'city' as per operation history
joined = pd.merge(source0, source1[['city', 'type']], on='city', how='inner')

# Select only the columns required in the target schema: ['city', 'type', 'fare']
# Ensure correct data types: city (string), type (string), fare (float)
result = joined[['city', 'type', 'fare']].copy()
result['city'] = result['city'].astype(str)
result['type'] = result['type'].astype(str)
result['fare'] = result['fare'].astype(float)

# Write the result to the specified path without the index
result.to_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_70/target_multisource.csv", index=False)

import pandas as pd

# Read source tables with index_col=0 to ignore the first numerical index column
source0 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_70/training_0.csv", index_col=0)
source1 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_70/training_1.csv", index_col=0)

# Join on 'city'
joined = pd.merge(source0, source1, on="city", how="inner")

# Group by 'city' and 'type' and aggregate fare by mean
result = joined.groupby(["city", "type"], as_index=False).agg({"fare": "mean"})

# Write output with exact target schema and column names
result.to_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_70/target_multisource_critique_history.csv", index=False)
